card.name: Hip Hop
card.tagline: The Bronx, 1973 — DJ Kool Herc's breakbeats turned a block party into a culture.
card.profile: Hip hop dance is a range of street dance styles primarily performed to hip hop music or that have evolved as part of hip hop culture. It is influenced by a wide range of styles that were created in the 1970s and made popular by dance crews in the United States. The television show Soul Train and the 1980s films Breakin', Beat Street, and Wild Style showcased these crews and dance styles in their early stages; therefore, giving hip-hop dance mainstream exposure.
card.insight: In its earliest form, it began as elaborations on James Brown's "Good Foot" dance, which debuted in 1972. In a 2001 interview Richard "Crazy Legs" Colón, the president of Rock Steady Crew, commented on how Puerto Ricans contributed to breaking: "I think the difference is when the brothas first started doing and it was at its infancy they weren't doing acrobatic moves.

parts.note: Teacher welcomes viewers and explains the tutorial structure
Teacher explains she will mirror movements and starts teaching legs
Teacher combines leg and arm movements together
Practice combined choreography with music at a slow tempo
Teacher adds the next part of the choreography

steps.name: Leg Taps and Cross Steps
steps.description: Tapping left and right feet out, then stepping across.

steps.name: Arm Extensions and Fists
steps.description: Stretching arms down, bending forearms, and punching to the side.

lessons.teacher_style: The instructor guides students through a step-by-step breakdown, starting with legs before adding arms and music. She maintains an encouraging and upbeat tone while repeating counts and gradual tempo progressions.
lessons.distinctive_method: Breaking down the upper and lower body movements completely independently before attempting any synchronization.
what_works: Isolating upper and lower body before combining them
Gradually increasing the tempo of practice
what_hinders: Lack of back-facing view makes learning complex turns or footwork harder to follow

evidence.observation: Teacher stands facing the camera in a studio setting, explaining foot placement while demonstrating mirrored steps.
Teacher demonstrates arm extensions downwards and bending forearms in parallel lines.
